# lean-pkg registry recommend

set the lean-pkg version this registry recommends; an older lean-pkg's writing commands then print a notice (offline; never a refusal).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry recommend [--reason REASON] [common flags] VERSION
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `VERSION` | X.Y.Z: the release every machine using this registry should run (stored as the top-level lean_pkg.recommended; event registry-recommended) |
| `--reason REASON` | free text recorded with the event |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `recommend VERSION` | set the release of lean-pkg every machine using this registry should run: the registry's optional top-level `lean_pkg: {recommended: X.Y.Z}` (additive: the schema stays version 3, and an older lean-pkg ignores the key and keeps it on every save), and the log-only event `registry-recommended` {`recommended`, `previous`, `reason`}. The same version again writes nothing (exit 0); a VERSION that is not `X.Y.Z` (three non-negative integers) exits 2. A write like any other: committed mode (`--commit`, `--push`) and the registry lock apply. `--json`: {ok, recommended, previous, registry, event (null when nothing was written), running} | `VERSION` `[--reason TEXT]` |

**The notice.** When the running lean-pkg is older than the recommendation, every writing command (every
registry write: `gate`, `lease claim`, `renew` and `release`, `register`, `update`, `record`, ...; and the
receipt producers `receipt slurm`, `systemd`, `ci` and `comparator`, outside their read-only forms
`--template`, `--check`, `--preflight-deps`, `--estimate`, `--verify-oleans` and `--attempts`) does its work and
then prints one line on stderr:

```text
lean-pkg: notice: this is lean-pkg 0.22.0; the registry recommends 0.23.0 (upgrade: pipx install --force 'git+https://github.com/lean-pkg/lean-pkg.git@v0.23.0')
```

The upgrade route is `git -C <checkout> pull --ff-only` for an editable install (a git checkout), else the
documented `pipx` install pinned to the recommended release's tag. It is never a refusal and never changes the
exit code, output or JSON otherwise; a registry write's `--json` payload gains `lean_pkg_skew` {`running`,
`recommended`}, absent when the running lean-pkg is not older. The check reads only the registry: no network.
Read-only commands stay silent; `doctor` shows the same comparison as its `recommended` line.

Versions compare on `X.Y.Z`: the running version's leading `X.Y.Z` is used, so an editable development build
(`0.23.0.dev1`, `0.23.0+dirty`) counts as 0.23.0, and a running version with no leading `X.Y.Z` is never older.
Equal or newer is silent. To stop the notice everywhere, recommend the release the lab runs.

## Examples

Record that every machine using this registry should run lean-pkg 0.23.0 (the top-level lean_pkg.recommended key and a registry-recommended event), committed with the registry.

```bash
lean-pkg registry recommend 0.23.0 --reason "lab on 0.23.0" --commit
```

Sample output:

```text
the registry recommends lean-pkg 0.23.0 (was 0.22.0); writing commands of an older lean-pkg print a notice (this is 0.23.0)
```
